approach: Add a `bug-evidence` default to defaults.toml. Add `ensure_bug_evidence(reading, request_text)` in reading.rs beside `ensure_changelog`, called from `build_reading` before `validate()`. For a `change` reading it adds one content criterion (data-backed root-cause evidence) and one `bug-evidence` defaults_applied entry, once. The trigger is two-tier. (1) The primary trigger is that the reader itself named `bug-evidence` in defaults_applied; it sees the new default's first sentence and judges semantically. (2) A narrow fallback is for a reader that skipped the default: bug-type words in the request text or the reading title, not the summary, with compounds like `bug-evidence` ignored, `regression test(s)` excluded, and a fix-intent word required. `build_reading` gains a `request_text: &str` argument from its one production caller. The reader set (1997 of 2000) goes over budget, so, following the `behavior-evidence` precedent (CHANGELOG.md:3035-3042), `BudgetSet::Reader` in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs is raised to the smallest multiple of 50 at or above the measured size. D25 in docs/decisions.md, the `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md, the pinned "of 2000" in run_pin_tests.rs and the quoted figures in context-engineer.md are updated. The three existing defaults `buy-first`, `public` and `verified` and `root-cause` stay untouched. Tests go in athena-core, athena-data and athena-context. CHANGELOG.md and defaults-loop.md record the change and its cause.

decisions.choice: Add the criterion and defaults entry in `build_reading` as a new step next to `ensure_changelog`, not as a refusal in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: Root cause: bug jobs were rejected at the final verdict because no criterion demanded data-backed root-cause evidence. A step guarantees the criterion without a model round trip. It refuses nothing, so there is no refusal rate to replay and no new `step!` line or corpus case. It follows `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:281-303): idempotent, capability-gated, run before `validate()` (reading.rs:842-843).

rejected.option: A `check_*` refusal in `refusing_check` that rejects a bug reading lacking the criterion
rejected.why: It adds a refusal rule (replay share, a corpus case that must refuse) and sends the reader round again for a sentence Athena can write itself.

rejected.option: Rely on the reader prompt and the default alone
rejected.why: Prose-only. The `mechanism` default asks for enforcement by mechanism.

decisions.choice: Two-tier trigger, applied only when `capability == Some("change")`. Tier 1: the reader's defaults_applied already holds `bug-evidence`, so the step guarantees the criterion. Tier 2 (fallback, adds the entry as well): `names_bug_work(request_text)` or `names_bug_work(title)` is true. `names_bug_work` lowercases and collapses whitespace, then requires BOTH a bug word and a fix-intent word in the same text. Bug words: `bug`, `bugs`, `bug-fix`, `bugfix`, `regression`, `regressions`, `slowdown`, `slowdowns`, `wrong output`, `wrong-output`. Fix-intent words: `fix`, `fixes`, `fixed`, `fixing`, `repair`, `repairs`, `diagnose`, `investigate`. An occurrence of a bug word counts only if the next character is not `-`, `_` or alphanumeric (so `bug-evidence` and `bug_id` do not count; the hyphenated phrases `bug-fix` and `wrong-output` are matched as whole phrases first), and an occurrence of `regression` followed by the word `test`, `tests` or `testing` is skipped. The summary is not read.
decisions.reason: The critic showed that plain `has_phrase` (reading.rs:4058-4064) treats `-` as a word break, so `bug` matches inside `bug-evidence` and this job's own title would trigger, and that `slowdowns` (HISTORY.txt:345 'Throughput review: flag median slowdowns and queue a request') and 'Add a regression test for X' are features that cannot meet a root-cause criterion. Tier 1 relies on the reader's semantic judgement. The fix-intent requirement removes the feature collisions that the bug word alone cannot tell apart. `class_of_work` is a closed list (athena.toml:128-129) with no bug class. `build_reading` has no request today (reading.rs:685-695), so one `&str` argument is added; its only callers are reading.rs:642 and the test helper at reading.rs:5630. Known limit: this job's own title ('... enforce root-cause criterion on bug') has no fix verb, so the fallback skips it; tier 1 covers it when the reader names the default. The limit goes in the doc comment and defaults-loop.md §3.9.

rejected.option: Bare `has_phrase` on title, summary and request text with BUG_WORDS
rejected.why: It matches `bug-evidence`, `regression test` and `slowdowns` in feature requests, which would then be judged against a root-cause criterion they cannot meet.

rejected.option: Add a `bug` class to `[classes]` in athena.toml
rejected.why: Adding a class is a job of its own, changes governance, and bug work is also code or tests.
A reader that never lists the default would escape the mechanism, which is the failure that left earlier bug jobs without the criterion.

decisions.choice: Idempotency by field. The defaults entry is added only if no entry has id `bug-evidence`. The criterion is skipped if (a) a criterion text already starts with the constant's lead phrase 'before any fix, the change states the root cause', or (b) the reader had named `bug-evidence` at call start AND already has a `content` criterion whose lowercase text contains `root cause` or `root-cause`. Otherwise it is added. Condition (b) is evaluated from the state at call start, before the step adds its own entry, so a second call finds the lead phrase and changes nothing.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 5: a reader that named the default and wrote its own root-cause criterion does not get a near-duplicate, and so does not cost the planner an extra demonstration (admission.rs:179-197 needs one demonstration per criterion). A reader that listed the default and wrote no such criterion still gets the criterion.

rejected.option: Skip both when the defaults entry exists
rejected.why: A reader that lists the default but writes no criterion would escape the mechanism.
It leaves a reader-written root-cause criterion and the step's own side by side.

decisions.choice: The criterion is `kind: content` with text: 'Before any fix, the change states the root cause, shows it from data the job can read (records, a code path or a failing case) and shows why the wrong output or metric change follows from it; a guess labelled as an estimate does not meet this.' No path, no 'only ... may change' wording, no producer-report wording.
decisions.reason: A content criterion is judged from the diff the verifier sees. `producer_evidence_phrase` (reading.rs:4068), `check_boundary_and_repo_files` and `limits_changed_files` do not fire on it, and `check_environment_reach` reads behavior criteria only. A test runs `refusing_check` on the built reading to prove it. A newcomer can tell what evidence is required (outcome-check default).

rejected.option: A behavior criterion that names a command
rejected.why: No single command shows root-cause evidence in general, and a behavior criterion triggers `check_code_survey` and `check_environment_reach`.

risks.risk: The fallback trigger misses a bug request with no listed bug word (for example 'fix the crash') and no reader-named default, or fires on a feature request that has both a bug word and a fix verb (for example 'fix the docs for the bug report form').
risks.mitigation: Tier 1 (the reader names the default) covers paraphrases, because the reader sees the default's first sentence. Tier 2 requires a bug word AND a fix-intent word, ignores compounds such as bug-evidence, skips 'regression test(s)', and reads only the request and the title, not the summary. The limits are in the doc comment and defaults-loop.md §3.9, and the negative table pins the realistic collisions.

risks.risk: The added criterion text trips an existing reading check (producer_evidence_phrase, limits_changed_files, boundary or repo-file checks) and refuses the whole reading.
risks.mitigation: The criterion is content kind with no path, no 'only ... may change' phrase and no producer-report wording; `bug_evidence_added_text_trips_no_refusal_check` runs `refusing_check` on the built reading.

risks.risk: The reader set is only 3 tokens under budget, so the new line cannot fit without a budget change; the raise could be seen as growing prompts without limit.
risks.mitigation: Raise by the measured amount only, in a multiple of 50, recorded in D25 and the CHANGELOG, with the producer and verifier sets unchanged (the new line is a defaults line, not in their sets). The first sentence of the default is kept short (about 70 characters).

risks.risk: A raised budget leaves stale figures in docs that no test reads (context-engineer.md, D25).
risks.mitigation: They are listed in dependents and files; step 10 greps the repo for '1997', '99.85' and 'of 2000' in the touched docs and crates and fixes each reader figure.

risks.risk: The step guarantees the criterion exists, not that the producer meets it; the final verdict is still the verifier's judgement, and the verifier's rejection logic is out of scope.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and §3.9 say so. The default's statement requires readable data and says an estimate-labelled guess does not meet it, so the verifier has an explicit test.

risks.risk: A retry request may quote earlier job text containing bug words and fix verbs, so the fallback fires on a retry of a non-bug job.
risks.mitigation: The criterion is judged by the verifier from the diff, and a retry of a bug job is the intended case. Tier 2 is the narrower tier; the quoted-job case is listed as a known limit in §3.9.

The test asserts that `build_reading`'s body contains `ensure_changelog(&mut reading)`, then `ensure_bug_evidence(&mut reading, request_text)`, then `reading.validate()`, in that order. It fails if the call is removed or moved after `validate()`.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests drive the real `Athena::build_reading` through a new helper with a bug request, plus the step directly, over a positive and negative input table. The tests cover both tiers, idempotency, the reader-supplied criterion path, and that the added text trips no `refusing_check` step. Realistic collisions are in the negative table.
demonstrations.observes: All `bug_evidence_*` tests pass. (a) A change reading built from 'Fix the bug where the report shows the wrong output' has exactly one content criterion starting 'Before any fix, the change states the root cause' and exactly one `bug-evidence` entry; `refusing_check` on it is None. (b) Fallback positives: 'Fix the regression in the parser', 'Investigate the slowdown in queue drain', 'Fix wrong-output in the status line', 'Fix the regression and add a regression test'. Fallback negatives, which get neither the criterion nor the entry: 'Add a regression test for the parser', 'Add bug-evidence default and enforce root-cause criterion on bug', 'Throughput review: flag median slowdowns and queue a request', 'Describe the demo in README.md', 'Add debug logging', a study-capability bug request, a declined reading. (c) Tier 1: a change reading whose request has no keyword but whose defaults_applied lists `bug-evidence` and has no root-cause criterion gains the criterion and no second entry. A reader that listed it AND wrote a content criterion containing 'root cause' gains nothing. A reader criterion that mentions root cause but whose reader did not list the default does get the step's criterion. (d) Calling the step twice leaves the reading equal.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no step, (a) finds zero root-cause criteria and zero `bug-evidence` entries. With bare `has_phrase` matching on title, summary and request, the negative table fails on 'bug-evidence', 'regression test' and 'slowdowns'. With a non-idempotent step, (d) finds duplicates. Without the capability gate, the study case gains the criterion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::build_reading` (reading.rs:685) through a new test helper `build_for_request(reading_json, request_text, capabilities)` added in step 8. It copies `build_sized` (reading.rs:5606-5640): `crate::test_support::make_athena` on tempdirs, the shipped athena.toml and defaults.toml, `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`, and capabilities ["change","study"]. The reading JSON comes from the existing `sized_reading` (reading.rs:5580) with capability set to change. The step is also called directly on the existing `change_reading()` (reading.rs:6130). No double holds the logic under test: the real `build_reading`, `names_bug_work` and `refusing_check` run.}
